touches.text: dataref: one address for any stored record, in any format, and the thin class that reads it. Shaped by Akien and CC 2026-11-09, grown from CC0AC-Weather 1.4.8's secrets.env. WHY: a config, a ticket or a node can say WHERE a value lives without carrying it, so the repo stays shareable and a private value stays in ~/.cairn; and one way of pointing works across every format and every box. USERS: anything that reads stored data.

cairn:/// is the repo (from the environment, or from where bin/cairn itself lives); cairncommons:/// is the commons repo beside it; instance:/// is ~/.cairn; claude:/// is ~/.claude (the project's own .claude/ is already cairn:///.claude/, so it gets no second name); db:///cairn/table/row is the database; file:/// keeps its usual meaning, a real path on the filesystem, for what no root holds. claude: is also the Claude app's link scheme on this box: the resolver never hands an address to the system, so only a click on one opens the app.
After #, names separated by /: #key (an env file), #section/key (an ini file), #a/b/c (into json).

secret: wraps any whole address and hands back what it points at as a Secret: secret:instance:///devices/cc/0/.env#githubtoken, secret:db:///cairn/t/row#token. Take off "secret:" and what is left is a complete address, whose # is its own. One colon, no //: a // says a host comes next, so secret://file://... would read "file" as a host. Precedent: jar:file:, view-source:https:. Akien 2026-11-09: "i like it. make it so".

Dataref is the base class. Secret is its subclass: its str, repr and format are all **********, so a log line or an f-string cannot show it; .secret fetches the value at that moment. WHY: printing it by mistake shows stars, and every place a secret is unmasked is a .secret anyone can grep for. Akien 2026-11-09. Prior art: pydantic's SecretStr, and fsspec for one interface over many stores (cited, not grafted).

A Dataref reads; it never writes. A write goes through the owner's gate (Law 6), and a db: address is read through db_domain's own client, never a second dial to 5432. An address on another box is read over the bus. WHY: one address system must not become one back door.

A file Dataref keeps its value and re-reads only when the file's modification time, size or inode has changed (a stat reads no data; a write that replaces the file in one step gets a new inode, which catches a change where timestamps are coarse). A Secret keeps nothing between reads. A db Dataref does not cache until a measured need asks for it. HYPOTHESIS: it will be read often enough for the cache to pay; the reads are counted (a metric, 17.27) to find out.
One that does not resolve is loud and names its address, never a value. A sieve reds a class-space config holding a plain value where a secret belongs.
Publishes a client tool (connect, read, write, query ...) that talks to the database over its socket, no bus hop: faster (2.3.7.1.1).
charter: compiles a component's bounded state from its history. WHY: state is compiled from the component's tickets, never hand-edited (Law 5). Held by CodeMother.

metric: records a measurement of anything. WHY: a metric is a primitive; its job is to measure whatever it is, and like feedback (which a metric strictly is) it must eventually have a consumer. USERS: any probe or tool.
